_comment: Guardian MCP set — Linear + GitHub + Slack baseline. Security scanners (gitleaks, trufflehog, snyk, osv-scanner), a11y tools (axe, lighthouse), perf tools (k6, artillery) are all Bash commands in settings.json — not MCPs. The LLM-as-judge mechanism used by the llm-security skill is router-mediated (a sub-session call), not an MCP. Verify package names before Phase 1 deploy.

_anthropic._comment: Anthropic API MCP — NOT WIRED. Declared because permissions.allow names `mcp__anthropic__judge_*`, the LLM-as-judge calls the `llm-security` skill uses for red-team scoring. A `_` prefix means planned and skipped by both activeServers() and collectInProcessMcp(). Distinct from Platform's `_anthropic_usage` (scoring vs billing). The key must equal the `mcp__<server>__` prefix used in permissions.

_linear._comment: Linear MCP — Guardian files security/qa/compliance/perf findings as Linear tickets, severity-labeled, routed to the relevant Builder (or human for legal-review). Adds Curator-relayed tickets when sensitive-paths.yml updates are needed.

github._comment: GitHub MCP — Guardian posts unified review comments on every PR, opens dep-CVE bump PRs (narrow remediation scope), opens PRs to dev-team to update sensitive-paths.yml when accepting candidates via the Sensitive-Paths Protocol. Guardian NEVER merges PRs (denied by settings.json).

slack._comment: Slack MCP — post P0 findings to #security; weekly llm-security summary to #security; monthly compliance audit summary to #compliance; weekly dep-CVE summary to #security.

_future_mcp_candidates._comment: Possible additions during Phase 5+. NOT enabled at v1.
_future_mcp_candidates.snyk: Snyk MCP could replace the Bash(snyk test:*) invocation with a richer query surface. Useful when Guardian needs to read historical scan data, not just run a new scan.
_future_mcp_candidates.sentry-readonly: If the project's app reports errors to Sentry, an MCP for reading recent production errors could enrich Guardian's review (e.g. 'this code path is implicated in a recurring prod error — flag harder').
_future_mcp_candidates.llm-as-judge-mcp: If LLM-as-judge gets used heavily by llm-security, wrapping it as a dedicated MCP server (rather than the router-mediated sub-session approach) could be cleaner. Performance/cost tradeoff — revisit after first 30 days.
